exchanges.subject: Peak safety bonus: change the measure before peak
exchanges.body: Lisa, this morning Shawn asked me to keep a prescription case off the log because the team's peak safety bonus is tied to recordables. I said no, but the bonus itself is the problem: an incentive that pays for fewer reported injuries discourages reporting, which OSHA's 1904.35 rules prohibit, and it costs us the early warnings. Proposal for peak: pay the same pool on leading indicators: safety huddles held, near misses reported, 5S and forklift pre-shift checks completed. Carmen and Andrea are copied; can we decide before the 11/9 start?

exchanges.author: c_ehsdir
exchanges.subject: Re: Peak safety bonus: change the measure before peak
exchanges.body: Fully agree. I'd add 'safety observations completed' as a fourth measure. Andrea and I can bring a version to Lisa by Thursday. Carmen

threads.title: Inbound call, Rick Dalton (Buckeye Columbus terminal)

exchanges.author: c_rick
exchanges.body: Ronan, Rick Dalton, I run Buckeye's Columbus terminal. Jasmine sent me your log on the Lexington pickups. Tell me what you're seeing so I can fix it.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Thanks for calling, Rick. Two of last week's five Lexington pickups missed the 4:00 window: Tuesday's GRV-88174 was picked up at 7:45 and Thursday's GRV-88290 at 8:30, so both delivered mid-afternoon instead of by 10. Friday's was on us. I need a 4:00 pickup we can count on, and a call by 3:30 if the driver is running late.

exchanges.author: c_rick
exchanges.body: We lost two drivers on that run in October. What I can guarantee is a 5:30 pickup every day. Would that work for you?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: 5:30 won't make a 10:00 delivery in Lexington reliably, so no. Keep the 4:00 pickup for this week, and send me in writing what you're changing to hold it. I'm also giving these dates to Scott Brenner for your quarterly review on 11/12.

exchanges.author: c_rick
exchanges.body: Fair. I'll put a dedicated driver on the Lexington run starting today and email you the plan this afternoon.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Rick Dalton (Buckeye Columbus terminal), 11/2: acknowledged the missed Lexington pickups on 10/27 (GRV-88174, 7:45) and 10/29 (GRV-88290, 8:30); short two drivers. Offered a guaranteed 5:30 pickup; declined, it misses the 10:00 Lexington delivery. Agreed: 4:00 pickup with a call by 3:30 if late; dedicated driver from today; written plan by this afternoon. For Scott's 11/12 quarterly review.

exchanges.body: Hi Ronan, it's Rosa on first shift. Tomorrow's Election Day and my polling place doesn't open until 6:30. Can I come in at 8:30 instead of 7 so I can vote? I don't want to get a point.

threads.title: Inbound call, Brett Lyons (Scioto Health kits)

exchanges.author: c_brett
exchanges.body: Ronan, it's Brett. Scioto Health wants us to kit their monthly PM parts, about 120 kits a month, fourteen lines a kit, bagged and labeled by building. Dana wants a number from me tomorrow. Can you just give me a ballpark per kit now? I'm thinking ten bucks.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: We can do it, but I won't guess a number. Under OPS-310 the price comes from a timed labor standard, so I'll have Kim time ten kits tomorrow and send you a written per-kit price by Wednesday. Please don't quote Dana anything before then.

exchanges.author: c_brett
exchanges.body: Okay. Wednesday is fine, she can wait two days. Send me the sample kit list I emailed?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Yes, send it to Kim and me tonight and she'll build the samples from it.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Brett Lyons, 11/2: Scioto Health wants about 120 PM kits a month, 14 lines each, bagged and labeled by building. Asked for a ballpark (he suggested $10); none given. Price per OPS-310 from a timed standard: Kim to time 10 sample kits Tuesday; written price to Brett by Wednesday. Brett sends the sample kit list tonight. He won't quote Dana before then.
